ComplexType.name: AssetInfo
ComplexType.Comment: Set of attributes of an asset, representing typical datasheet information of a physical device that can be instantiated and shared in different data exchange contexts:
- as attributes of an asset instance (installed or in stock)
- as attributes of an asset model (product by a manufacturer)
- as attributes of a type asset (generic type of an asset as used in designs/extension planning).

EnumeratedType.name: CrewStatusKind
EnumeratedType.Comment: Defines the current status of the Crew - assigned, arrived, etc.

EnumeratedValue.name: arrived
EnumeratedValue.Comment: the crew is on site at the outage location

EnumeratedValue.name: assigned
EnumeratedValue.Comment: the crew has been assigned to work on a task

EnumeratedValue.name: awaitingCrewAssignment
EnumeratedValue.Comment: Indicates that the work is awaiting one or more crews to be assigned

EnumeratedValue.name: enroute
EnumeratedValue.Comment: the crew has been dispatched to work on an outage

EnumeratedValue.name: fieldComplete
EnumeratedValue.Comment: the crew has corrected the outage in the field. The equipment or other devices may not be energized at this time.

Simple.name: email1
Simple.Comment: Primary email address.

Simple.name: email2
Simple.Comment: Alternate email address.

Simple.name: lan
Simple.Comment: Address on local area network.

Simple.name: mac
Simple.Comment: MAC (Media Access Control) address.

Simple.name: password
Simple.Comment: Password needed to log in.

Simple.name: radio
Simple.Comment: Radio address.

Simple.name: userID
Simple.Comment: User ID needed to log in, which can be for an individual person, an organisation, a location, etc.

Simple.name: web
Simple.Comment: World wide web address.

ComplexType.name: IdentifiedObject
ComplexType.Comment: This is a root class to provide common identification for all classes needing identification and naming attributes.

Simple.name: mRID
Simple.Comment: Master resource identifier issued by a model authority. The mRID is unique within an exchange context. Global uniqueness is easily achieved by using a UUID, as specified in RFC 4122, for the mRID. The use of UUID is strongly recommended.
For CIMXML data files in RDF syntax conforming to IEC 61970-552, the mRID is mapped to rdf:ID or rdf:about attributes that identify CIM object elements.

Simple.name: name
Simple.Comment: The name is any free human readable and possibly non unique text naming the object.

Root.name: Name
Root.Comment: The Name class provides the means to define any number of human readable names for an object. A name is not to be used for defining inter-object relationships. For inter-object relationships instead use the object identification 'mRID'.

Simple.name: name
Simple.Comment: Any free text that name the object.

Reference.name: IdentifiedObject
Reference.Comment: Identified object that this name designates.

InverseReference.name: Names
InverseReference.Comment: All names of this identified object.

Root.name: Organisation
Root.Comment: Organisation that might have roles as utility, contractor, supplier, manufacturer, customer, etc.

InverseInstance.name: Organisation
InverseInstance.Comment: Organisation that is part of this parent organisation.

Compound.name: postalAddress
Compound.Comment: Postal address, potentially different than 'streetAddress' (e.g., another city).

EnumeratedType.name: PhaseCode
EnumeratedType.Comment: An unordered enumeration of phase identifiers. Allows designation of phases for both transmission and distribution equipment, circuits and loads. The enumeration, by itself, does not describe how the phases are connected together or connected to ground. Ground is not explicitly denoted as a phase.

Residential and small commercial loads are often served from single-phase, or split-phase, secondary circuits. For the example of s12N, phases 1 and 2 refer to hot wires that are 180 degrees out of phase, while N refers to the neutral wire. Through single-phase transformer connections, these secondary circuits may be served from one or two of the primary phases A, B, and C. For three-phase loads, use the A, B, C phase codes instead of s12N.
The integer values are from IEC 61968-9 to support revenue metering applications.

EnumeratedValue.name: ABCN
EnumeratedValue.Comment: Phases A, B, C, and N.

EnumeratedValue.name: XYN
EnumeratedValue.Comment: Two unknown non-neutral phases plus neutral.

CompoundType.name: Status
CompoundType.Comment: Current status information relevant to an entity.

Simple.name: dateTime
Simple.Comment: Date and time for which status 'value' applies.

Simple.name: reason
Simple.Comment: Reason code or explanation for why an object went to the current status 'value'.

Simple.name: remark
Simple.Comment: Pertinent information regarding the current 'value', as free form text.

Simple.name: value
Simple.Comment: Status value at 'dateTime'; prior status changes may have been kept in instances of activity records associated with the object to which this status applies.

CompoundType.name: StreetAddress
CompoundType.Comment: General purpose street and postal address information.

Simple.name: language
Simple.Comment: The language in which the address is specified, using ISO 639-1 two digit language code.

Simple.name: poBox
Simple.Comment: Post office box.

Simple.name: postalCode
Simple.Comment: Postal code for the address.

CompoundType.name: StreetDetail
CompoundType.Comment: Street details, in the context of address.

Simple.name: addressGeneral
Simple.Comment: First line of a free form address or some additional address information (for example a mail stop).

Simple.name: addressGeneral2
Simple.Comment: (if applicable) Second line of a free form address.

Simple.name: addressGeneral3
Simple.Comment: (if applicable) Third line of a free form address.

Simple.name: buildingName
Simple.Comment: (if applicable) In certain cases the physical location of the place of interest does not have a direct point of entry from the street, but may be located inside a larger structure such as a building, complex, office block, apartment, etc.

Simple.name: code
Simple.Comment: (if applicable) Utilities often make use of external reference systems, such as those of the town-planner's department or surveyor general's mapping system, that allocate global reference codes to streets.

Simple.name: floorIdentification
Simple.Comment: The identification by name or number, expressed as text, of the floor in the building as part of this address.

Simple.name: name
Simple.Comment: Name of the street.

Simple.name: number
Simple.Comment: Designator of the specific location on the street.

Simple.name: prefix
Simple.Comment: Prefix to the street name. For example: North, South, East, West.

Simple.name: suffix
Simple.Comment: Suffix to the street name. For example: North, South, East, West.

Simple.name: suiteNumber
Simple.Comment: Number of the apartment or suite.

Simple.name: type
Simple.Comment: Type of street. Examples include: street, circle, boulevard, avenue, road, drive, etc.

Simple.name: withinTownLimits
Simple.Comment: True if this street is within the legal geographical boundaries of the specified town (default).

Simple.name: areaCode
Simple.Comment: (if applicable) Area or region code.

Simple.name: cityCode
Simple.Comment: City code.

Simple.name: countryCode
Simple.Comment: Country code.

Simple.name: dialOut
Simple.Comment: (if applicable) Dial out code, for instance to call outside an enterprise.

Simple.name: extension
Simple.Comment: (if applicable) Extension for this telephone number.

Simple.name: internationalPrefix
Simple.Comment: (if applicable) Prefix used when calling an international number.

Simple.name: ituPhone
Simple.Comment: Phone number according to International Telecommunication Union (ITU) E.164.

Simple.name: localNumber
Simple.Comment: Main (local) part of this telephone number.

CompoundType.name: TownDetail
CompoundType.Comment: Town details, in the context of address.

Simple.name: code
Simple.Comment: Town code.

Simple.name: country
Simple.Comment: Name of the country.

Simple.name: name
Simple.Comment: Town name.

Simple.name: section
Simple.Comment: Town section. For example, it is common for there to be 36 sections per township.

Simple.name: stateOrProvince
Simple.Comment: Name of the state or province.

Root.name: WireInfo
Root.Comment: Wire data that can be specified per line segment phase, or for the line segment as a whole in case its phases all have the same wire characteristics.

Domain.name: coreRadius
Domain.Comment: (if there is a different core material) Radius of the central core.

Simple.name: coreStrandCount
Simple.Comment: (if used) Number of strands in the steel core.

Domain.name: gmr
Domain.Comment: Geometric mean radius. If we replace the conductor by a thin walled tube of radius GMR, then its reactance is identical to the reactance of the actual conductor.

Simple.name: insulated
Simple.Comment: True if conductor is insulated.

Enumerated.name: insulationMaterial
Enumerated.Comment: (if insulated conductor) Material used for insulation.

Domain.name: insulationThickness
Domain.Comment: (if insulated conductor) Thickness of the insulation.

EnumeratedValue.name: asbestosAndVarnishedCambric
EnumeratedValue.Comment: Asbestos and varnished cambric wire insulation.

EnumeratedValue.name: highMolecularWeightPolyethylene
EnumeratedValue.Comment: High nolecular weight polyethylene wire insulation.

EnumeratedValue.name: highPressureFluidFilled
EnumeratedValue.Comment: High pressure fluid filled wire insulation.

EnumeratedValue.name: treeResistantHighMolecularWeightPolyethylene
EnumeratedValue.Comment: Tree resistant high molecular weight polyethylene wire insulation.

EnumeratedValue.name: treeRetardantCrosslinkedPolyethylene
EnumeratedValue.Comment: Tree retardant crosslinked polyethylene wire insulation.

Root.name: WireSpacingInfo
Root.Comment: Wire spacing data that associates multiple wire positions with the line segment, and allows to calculate line segment impedances. Number of phases can be derived from the number of associated wire positions whose phase is not neutral.

SimpleType.name: Length
SimpleType.Comment: Unit of length. It shall be a positive value or zero.

PrimitiveType.name: Boolean
PrimitiveType.Comment: A type with the value space "true" and "false".

PrimitiveType.name: DateTime
PrimitiveType.Comment: Date and time as "yyyy-mm-ddThh:mm:ss.sss", which conforms with ISO 8601. UTC time zone is specified as "yyyy-mm-ddThh:mm:ss.sssZ". A local timezone relative UTC is specified as "yyyy-mm-ddThh:mm:ss.sss-hh:mm". The second component (shown here as "ss.sss") could have any number of digits in its fractional part to allow any kind of precision beyond seconds.

PrimitiveType.name: Integer
PrimitiveType.Comment: An integer number. The range is unspecified and not limited.

PrimitiveType.name: String
PrimitiveType.Comment: A string consisting of a sequence of characters. The character encoding is UTF-8. The string length is unspecified and unlimited.

Package.name: AssetInfo
Package.Comment: This package is an extension of Assets package and contains the core information classes that support asset management and different network and work planning applications with specialized AssetInfo subclasses. They hold attributes that can be referenced by not only Asset-s or AssetModel-s but also by ConductingEquipment-s.

Package.name: Assets
Package.Comment: This package contains the core information classes that support asset management applications that deal with the physical and lifecycle aspects of various network resources (as opposed to power system resource models defined in IEC61970::Wires package, which support network applications).

Package.name: Base
Package.Comment: Content of the base CIM published as IEC 61970-301.

Package.name: Common
Package.Comment: This package contains the information classes that support distribution management in general.

Package.name: Core
Package.Comment: Contains the core PowerSystemResource and ConductingEquipment entities shared by all applications plus common collections of those entities. Not all applications require all the Core entities. This package does not depend on any other package except the Domain package, but most of the other packages have associations and generalizations that depend on it.

Package.name: Domain
Package.Comment: The domain package defines primitive datatypes that are used by classes in other packages. Stereotypes are used to describe the datatypes. The following stereotypes are defined:
<<enumeration>> A list of permissible constant values.
<<Primitive>> The most basic data types used to compose all other data types.

<<CIMDatatype>> A datatype that contains a value attribute, an optional unit of measure and a unit multiplier. The unit and multiplier may be specified as a static variable initialized to the allowed value.
<<Compound>> A composite of Primitive, enumeration, CIMDatatype or other Compound classes, as long as the Compound classes do not recurse.
For all datatypes both positive and negative values are allowed unless stated otherwise for a particular datatype.

Package.name: IEC61968
Package.Comment: The IEC 61968 subpackages of the CIM are developed, standardized and maintained by the UCA community including its working groups and task forces.
Currently, normative parts of the model support the needs of information exchange defined in IEC 61968-3, IEC 61968-4, IEC 61968-5, IEC 61968-6, IEC 61968-8, IEC 61968-9 and in IEC 61968-13.

Package.name: TC57CIM
Package.Comment: Top package for IEC TC57 CIM.
